description: First generated batch: 20 countries that test the pipeline across every continent before a larger run.
selection: Every inhabited continent is covered, with four or five countries each from Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas and two from Oceania, plus Greenland for the Arctic.
The 10 countries with reviewed content (BRA, CHN, FRA, IND, IDN, JPN, MYS, SGP, TUR, USA) are left out so the pilot only produces new drafts.
Most picks are countries curious readers ask about often, so drafts can be judged against what people actually want to know.
A few picks stress the map: long sea routes (CHL, AUS, NZL), canals the gazetteer lacks (PAN, EGY), huge land countries (RUS, KAZ, CAN) and a remote Arctic island (GRL).
Neighbours and partners are grouped (EGY and SAU, ARG and CHL, AUS and NZL, CAN and MEX) so the batch plan can link questions across countries inside the pilot.

countries.why: The Nile, the Suez Canal and a very old state: rivers, chokepoints and history in one country.
Africa's most populous country, with oil, many languages and a fast-growing cultural export.
East Africa's hub: the Rift Valley, running, mobile money and the Indian Ocean coast.
Three capitals, many official languages and a mining economy shaped by its history.
An island state whose language, law and former empire reach everywhere else in the atlas.
Europe's largest economy, its rivers and its federal, reunified story.
The largest country: many time zones, an Arctic coast and pipelines that link it to many others.
Land made from sea, Rotterdam's port and a small country with outsized trade.
A divided peninsula that became a technology and culture exporter within one lifetime.
Oil, deserts and coasts on the Red Sea and the Gulf; pairs with Egypt across the Red Sea.
The largest landlocked country: steppe, a space launch site and Silk Road crossings.
A long coast on the South China Sea, the Mekong delta and a manufacturing boom.
A vast northern country of lakes, Arctic passages and a long border with the United States.
Ancient cities, a border that shapes two economies and food the world borrows.
The long thin country: the Andes, the Atacama, copper and a very long Pacific coast.
The canal between two oceans; tests how the map draws a passage the gazetteer does not have.
The pampas, Patagonia and Buenos Aires; pairs with Chile across the Andes.
An island continent: deserts, the Great Barrier Reef, mining and long sea links to Asia.
Two main islands far from everything, plate boundaries, and Maori and settler history.
The largest island, its ice sheet and Arctic routes; a territory with its own content file.
